msItem.title: Note of the contents of the manuscript
msItem.incipit: In this present treatise folowinge your grace maye vnderstande all maner of service that all the noble lordes of this realme be bounde to do vnto their prince as well at the tyme of his coronacion as other tymes ... Also this present booke maketh mencion of all the manner forme & kepinge of the parlemente of Englande ... Also this booke maketh mencion of the honurable office of Constable & Marshall of Englande ... .

msItem.title: The coronation of Richard II
msItem.rubric: The proces done or made at the coronacion of Kynge Richarde the seconde after the deathe of Kynge Edwarde the iijd after the conqueste
msItem.incipit: The moste fortunable blessed stronge & myghtye Edwarde kynge of Englande and of Fraunce by the disposicion of the divine power departed from this present liff the xjth day of June the yeare of our lorde God M.CCC.lxxvij and in the lj yeare of his raigne
msItem.explicit: to departe the which was diffuse to be obteyned not withstandyinge it was graunted and everye man departed
msItem.finalRubric: Thus endeth the solempnitie of the coronacion of kinge Richard the seconde after ye conqueste
msItem.note: A translation from the official record (in Latin and French) Processus factus ad coronationem Domini Regis Anglie Ricardi Secundi post conquestum anno regni sui primo (beg. 'Decedente de nutu ...'; Coronation Records, ed. Legg, pp. 131-150), which combines a record of the court of claims at Richard II's coronation with an account of the coronation itself. Wells Rev. 8:2704, 2938–39 [89].

Other texts: Wells Rev. lists 16 MSS in total (including this one). Add Oxf Exeter College 92, ff. 5–25 (see IMEP 8, [1]), and delete both Ashmole 863, which is an account of the coronation of Richard III, and Camb Caius 537/301. Versions previously indexed: IMEP 19, CUL Ee.4.37 [3] and Mm.3.29 [2]; IMEP 23, Rawl. B. 131 [1].

msItem.title: The Office of the Constable and Marshal of England
msItem.rubric: These be the rightes belonginge to the constable and marshall of Englande
msItem.incipit: The erle marshall ought to haue the kinges horse with all the harneys that is on him and the queenes palfrey when the light at the place where the shal be crowned. Therle ought to be always neerest ye kinge at his coronacion and ought to holde the crowne
msItem.explicit: of inferiors religeouse persons to take after the rate of their tenure and of other religeouse persons that holde but of almes to haue nothinge.
msItem.note: Apparently a composite text deriving from a dossier on the marshal and constable in Latin and French said to have been compiled for Thomas de Brotherton (d. 1338) and printed (from MS. Cotton Nero B. VI) in Joseph Edmonson, A Complete Body of Heraldry I (London, 1780), pp. 74-81 (headed 'Ces sont les usages que Thomas de Brotherton filz au roy clamoit a user pro l'office mareschalsie'). Fols. 17r-20r (line 9 from bottom) translate the French text pr. ibid. pp. 76-79 (beg. 'Le conte Mareschal doit avoir le palefrey ...'). Fols. 20r-21v (line 13 from bottom), beginning 'Also it is right that the constable and marshall haue the number of the man of armes and the names ...', translate the French text pr. ibid. pp. 74-5 (beg. 'Ensement il est droit ...'). Fols. 21v-22v, beginning 'In the tyme of peace the marshalles office is to deliuer or assigne lodginges ...' translate part of a Latin text pr. ibid. pp. 75-76 (beg. 'Tempore autem pacis est officium ...', ending p. 76 col. a '... nichil exigat Marescall.').

Other copies: IMEP 8, indexing Ex 92 [2], lists BL Harley 369; London, Society of Antiquaries 58; CUL Mm.3.29; olim Leconfield MS 17 (sold Sotheby’s 23 April 1928 lot 64; later belonging to Boies Penrose (d. 1976), see de Ricci, Census) . CUL Mm.3.29 is indexed IMEP 19. Add Rawl. B. 131, indexed IMEP 23, which notes a 17th-century copy in Ashmole 865, pp. 254-7, not separately indexed IMEP 9.

msItem.rubric: The manner and forme howe Thomas erle of Nottingham had ye marshallship of Englande by the kinges lettres patentes the tenour wherof hereafter ensuithe
msItem.note: Other copies: CUL Mm.3.29 (s. xv), indexed IMEP 19, with letters in Latin; Rawl. B. 131, fol. 9v (IMEP 23), letters in French; Harley MS. 369.

msItem.title: Ordinances of War at Durham, 1385 (Durham Ordinances)
msItem.rubric: Thes be the statutes ordenaunces and custumes to be holden in the hoste ordeyned and made by good advysement and deliberacion of our moste excellent souueraigne lorde Kinge Richard and John Duke of Lancaster stewarde of Englande beinge at Duresyn the xvijth day of the monthe of June the ixth yeare of the raigne of our souueraigne lorde kinge Richarde the Seconde
msItem.incipit: Furste that all manner of people of what nacion estate or condicion they be of be obeysant to our saide souueraigne lorde the kinge to his cunstable and marshall vpon payne of forfetinge of body and goodes. Also that no man so hardy to touche the sacrament of the aulter nor the pix
msItem.explicit: if any cometh and taketh lodginge and his name be not delyvered to the constable and marshall he shall lose his horse and harneis.
msItem.note: Translated from a French original (which is printed from Cotton Nero D. VI in Black Book of the Admiralty, ed. Twiss, I, pp. 453-8). For discussion see M. H. Keen, ‘Richard II’s ordinances of war of 1385’, in R. E. Archer and S. Walker (eds), Rulers and Ruled in Late Medieval England: Essays Presented to Gerald Harriss (London, 1995), pp. 33–48; Andrew Martinez, ‘Disciplinary Ordinances for English Armies and Military Change, 1385–1513’, History, vol. 102, no. 3 (351), 2017, pp. 361–85.
Other copies: CUL Mm.3.29 (s. xv), indexed IMEP 19; Rawl. B. 131, fol. 10r-v, indexed IMEP 23; Harley MS. 369.

msItem.title: Order of Battle in Scotland, 1385
msItem.rubric: The viage of kinge Edward into Scotlande
msItem.incipit: These be the ordenaunces of the iij battailles and the ij wynges of the kinges battaill at the first viage into Scotlande the ixth yere of his reigne. In the forwarde. The Duke of Lancaster - m men of armes - 3000 archers. The Erle of Buckyngham - 400 men of armes - 800 archers. The Erle of Nottingham - 200 men of armes - 300 archers
msItem.explicit: for ij winges of the kinges battell - j For other noble men of the kinges battell - ij. For the third battell - ij.
msItem.note: Pr. Nicholas Harris Nicolas, 'An account of the army with which King Richard the Second invaded Scotland ...', Archaeologia 22 (1829), 13-19, from BL Harley MS. 369, Harley MS. 1309, and MS. Ashmole 865.

Despite the rubric, the text relates to Richard II's army in 1385, and is again translated from a French original, printed from Cotton Nero D. VI fols. 91v-92r by S. Armitage-Smith, John of Gaunt (1904), pp. 437-439 (listing at p. 439 other manuscripts in the British Library). The French text is discussed by N. B. Lewis, 'The Last Medieval Summons of the English Feudal Levy, 13 June 1385', EHR, 73 (1958), 1–26.
Other copies: CUL Mm.3.29 (s. xv), indexed IMEP 19; MS. Harl. 369, fols. 92r-93r (s. xvi); MS. Harl. 1309 (s. xvii/xviii); MS. Ashmole 865 (s. xvii)

msItem.title: The Progress of King Edward I in his Invasion of Scotland (1296)
msItem.rubric: Here foloweth the viage of Kinge Edward into Scotland with all his lodginges brieflye expressed
msItem.incipit: In the xxiiij yere of the reigne of Kinge Edwarde Easter day was on the day of thannuntiacion of our ladye and on Tuesday in Easter weeke, beinge the xxviij day of March, passed Kinge Edward the fore nowne ye ryver of Twed with v thousand horses covered and thirtye thousand footemen, and lay that night in Scotland
msItem.explicit: came Tuisday to Coldingham, Wensday to Barwick and conquered it and serched the kingdome of Scotlande as is aforsaid in one and twentie weekes without anie more
msItem.note: Wells Rev. 8:2904 [54]; a translation from a French original which follows the preceding items in BL. Add. MSS. 29901 and 32097 .

Other copies: CUL Mm.3.29 (s. xv), indexed IMEP 19, which, following Wells Rev., lists other copies (s. xvi, s. xvii) in BL Add 5758 ff. 199–200; BL Harley 1309 ff. 39v–42v; and MS. Ashmole 865 pp. 254–7, not indexed in IMEP 9; add Rawl. B. 131, fols. 11v-12r, indexed IMEP 23.

msItem.title: Modus tenendi parliamentorum
msItem.rubric: Here ffoloweth the forme & maner of kepinge of the Parliament of Englande
msItem.incipit: The monicion or sommons of ye parliament ought to be made or done xl dayes before ye begynnynge of the parliament. For the Spiritualtie. All archbisshoppes, bisshoppes, abbottes, priours and all other greate clerkes that holde by countie or baronye by reason of theire holding they ought to be monisshed and also ought to come to the parliament and none other inferiours of the clergye vnlesse their presence were profitable
msItem.explicit: v dayes after the beginnynge of the parleament. Off ye preachinge at ye parleament.
msItem.note: Ends imperfect with the heading for section X

The English translation of the earlier or B recension. N. Pronay and J. Taylor, Parliamentary Texts of the Later Middle Ages (Oxford, 1980), p. 205, list three early manuscripts of this translation: Cambridge University Library MS. Mm.3.29 (s. xv), indexed IMEP 19; BL Addit. MS. 15091 (s. xvi); Society of Antiquaries MS. 58 (s. xv), and a further 15 later 'transcripts' (not including ours) including MS. Ashmole 865 (not separately indexed in IMEP 9) and MS. Bodl. 966 (s. xvii); add MS. Rawl. A. 78, MS. Rawl. B. 131 (both indexed IMEP 23); and Oxford, Exeter College, MS. 92 (indexed IMEP 8).
Fols. 34r-41v are blank. Fol. 34 was later used as the mount for a reproduction of British Library, Harley MS. 1319, fol. 57r (miniature of the deposition parliament from Jean Creton's Chronicle).
